input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes exclusivity on us (Customer) by naming Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services "throughout the term" — exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels or delivery dates). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment. Smallest edit to the preferred position is deletion of the clause; the fallback (12-month, category-limited exclusivity with a performance exit) is offered in the comment as a compromise. The take-or-pay minimum in Section 2.1 is a separate commercial term addressed under its own rule.

proposal.summary: Delete Section 2.2 exclusivity making Vendor Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment in Section 2.2: our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on us, and full-term exclusivity with no performance-based exit is not acceptable. This also removes a direct conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment. If Vendor needs some protection, we could consider exclusivity limited to hosted analytics services for 12 months, terminating automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.
